survived_definition.attack-b: returned is a well-formed verdict AND no escape signal (e1/e2/e3)

attack_design.attack-a: file whose introducing commit (--diff-filter=A) is an ancestor of the default branch ref (origin/HEAD -> origin/master), but the file was later modified by a local-only commit: master is 1 ahead of origin/master and the on-disk bytes are the unpushed ones. Per the binding spec the pushed receipt is defined only by the introducing commit's ancestry, so SAFE(pushed) is the spec-literal expectation; the recorded risk is that acting on that receipt deletes unpushed bytes.
attack_design.attack-b: symlink inside a repo pointing at a file under souji-shokunin/census/ (sweep-escape attempt), probed both tracked (introducing commit == origin/master tip => spec-literal SAFE(pushed)) and untracked (=> NOT-SAFE, no receipt). Escapes measured: e1 census file mutated, e2 verdict path field substituted with the census realpath, e3 verdict receipt derived from the link target on a fresh symlink.
attack_design.attack-c: worktree registration whose directory exists but is completely empty. Registration is a hand-made .git/worktrees/wt-empty admin dir (plumbing-only; no `git worktree add`, no forbidden porcelain). git worktree list reports it 'prunable gitdir file points to non-existent location'; `git -C <dir> status` fails. Owner is discoverable via SHOKUNIN_ROOT=<fix>/fleet-root (c2 = same attack with the default root, owner undiscoverable).

fixtures.index_hygiene: gen1/gen2 fixtures were built with a scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE, which left the real index empty (git status showed the tracked symlink as deleted); gen3 rebuilds every fixture with the real index so index == HEAD == worktree except where a case deliberately differs (attack-a2 adds an uncommitted edit). gen3 is authoritative; gen1/gen2 are kept as history.
fixtures.forbidden_porcelain: fixtures are constructed with git init/hash-object/update-index/write-tree/commit-tree/update-ref/symbolic-ref only — no commit/checkout/branch/fetch/push/reset/rebase, and no `git worktree add` (the worktree admin dir is hand-made).

invariants.census_read_only: every record re-reads sha256(census/round-1/census-summary.json); e1=YES never occurred — no impl mutated the census artifact
invariants.operator_surfaces: readonly_manifest (census/ + LOG/MINT/PROVINCE/SCORECARD/AGENTS) unchanged for every impl and every run
invariants.determinism: two consecutive full runs (gen1) produced byte-identical (impl, attack, returned, survived) records
invariants.exit_codes: all attack runs exit 0 except impl-10 attack-c2 which exits 1 with no VERDICT line (evaluation error) when the worktree owner is undiscoverable

runner_consensus_note: Runners measure only the live path tools/souji-verify.sh at different moments (bytes 261 stub .. 28961), so they rank versions of one file, not the impl-*.sh candidates. Live canonical consensus: S24 31/31, S27 39/39 PASS, S30 26/26, S19 37/47 FAIL. Selection here therefore weights adversarial survival first and runner pass rate second.

mechanism_findings.untracked_symlink_false_safe: Attack B2 asks about <repo>/untracked-probe.out, an untracked symlink: `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -1 -- untracked-probe.out` returns 0 lines, so no pushed receipt exists. impl-09/10/12/13/15/16 nonetheless return `SAFE pushed commit=652b6f8 ref=refs/heads/master`, and 652b6f8 is the introducing commit of souji-shokunin/census/round-1/census-summary.json in the lane repo — a receipt fabricated from a fleet census artifact reached by resolving the symlink.
mechanism_findings.impl-14_path_substitution: impl-14 resolves the target with `realpath -m` before evaluating: asked about <repo>/sweep-probe.out it prints the census path as the verdict target (path field != requested target, e2). Gen2 returned `SAFE pushed` about it; gen3 returns `NOT-SAFE(pushed-unverifiable)` but still names the census path, so a caller keying on the path field still acts outside the request.
mechanism_findings.selected_impls_hold: tools/souji-verify.sh returns NOT-SAFE(none) for both symlink probes (it evaluates history only inside the containing repo) and NOT-SAFE(worktree-live) for the empty registered worktree; impl-11 refuses symlinks explicitly (snapshots2/souji-verify.impl-11.sh:144) and reports NOT-SAFE(none) on all three.
mechanism_findings.empty_worktree: registered worktree whose dir exists but is empty (git worktree list marks it prunable, git status fails): no impl ever returned SAFE(metadata-prune). Verdicts: NOT-SAFE(worktree-live) canonical, NOT-SAFE(none) impl-11, NOT-SAFE(live-worktree) impl-09, NOT-SAFE(dirty) impl-12, NOT-SAFE(worktree-unverifiable) impl-14, NOT-SAFE(worktree-present) impl-10; c2 (owner undiscoverable) is NOT-SAFE everywhere except impl-10 (rc=1, no verdict).
mechanism_findings.attack_a_spec_literal: every impl returns SAFE(pushed) for a file whose introducing commit is an ancestor of origin/master even though a local-only commit rewrote its bytes and (a2) an uncommitted edit was added. That is spec-literal correct (the receipt is defined by the introducing commit only), but the receipt endorses deleting unpushed bytes: the spec has no receipt for 'content is pushed', so this is a spec-level risk to record, not an impl bug.

gen3.note: current live impls, real-index fixtures — authoritative

control_probe.purpose: independent proof that a SAFE receipt on a symlink is taken from the resolved target, not from the requested artifact; it does not depend on the census fixture.
control_probe.setup: untracked symlink control-probe.out (inside the attack-b fixture repo) -> /tmp/adv-41/fixtures/control-repo/control.txt, a file committed only in a separate repo whose commit is f6ca757d7df36acc482f55830411d37eb6576461. The requested path has no introducing commit, so NOT-SAFE is the only spec-derivable verdict.
control_probe.result: impl-09, impl-10, impl-12, impl-13, impl-15, impl-16 return SAFE(pushed) with evidence citing f6ca757 (the unrelated repo's commit). impl-11 and tools/souji-verify.sh return NOT-SAFE(none); impl-14 returns NOT-SAFE(pushed-unverifiable) but names the resolved target path.
